source.author: verg
source.text: Namque mihi, fallax haud ante repertus, hoc uno responso animum delusit Apollo, qui fore te ponto incolumem, finesque canebat venturum Ausonios.
source.text_original: Namque mihi, fallax haud ante repertus, / hoc uno responso animum delusit Apollo, / qui fore te ponto incolumem, finesque canebat / venturum Ausonios.
source.text_english: For Apollo, deceitful and never before discovered by me to be so, tricked my mind with this one reply alone, when he was foretelling that you would be safe on the sea and would come to the Ausonian shores.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hinc in terras latumque profundum est iter, hinc olim soliti miscere polumque infelixque fretum neque enim tune Aeolus illis rector erat, Libya cum rumperet advena Calpen Oceanus, cum flens Siculos Oenotria fines perderet et mediis intrarent montibus undae, intonuit donec pavidis ex aethere ventis omnipotens regemque dedit, quem iussa vereri saeva cohors: vix monte chalybs iterataque muris saxa domant Euros.
reuse.text_original: hinc in terras latumque profundum / est iter, hinc olim soliti miscere polumque / infelixque fretum (neque enim tune Aeolus illis / rector erat, Libya cum rumperet advena Calpen / Oceanus, cum flens Siculos Oenotria fines / perderet et mediis intrarent montibus undae), / intonuit donec pavidis ex aethere ventis / omnipotens regemque dedit, quem iussa vereri / saeva cohors: vix monte chalybs iterataque muris / saxa domant Euros.
reuse.text_english: from here the journey is over land and deep sea, from here, once wont to mingle sky and luckless strait; for then Aeolus was not ruler over them, when the Ocean, an intruder, was breaking Calpe apart from Libya, when Oenotria, weeping, was losing the Sicilian borders, and the waves were entering among the mountain ranges, until the almighty thundered from the sky at the fearful winds and gave them a king, whom the savage band is bound to obey: scarcely do iron and the stones of the walls, doubled by the mountain, subdue the Eura.
